brief:
Write a program that reports which words in a text repeat.

A word is a run of letters, digits, or apostrophes. Everything else separates words. Case is ignored, so "Report" and "report" are the same word.

Print one line for each word that appears at least twice, as the word, a single space, then the number of times it appears. Sort the lines by count, highest first, and break ties alphabetically, ascending. If no word repeats, print nothing.

For example, this input:

    the crane lifted the cargo, and the crane lowered it

produces this output:

    the 3
    crane 2

- Write the program to the file "solution.js".
- It will be run as `node solution.js` with no arguments, in a directory containing only the files you left there.
- Read the input from standard input, and write the result to standard output.
- Compare output exactly. Trailing whitespace at the very end is ignored; everything else is not.
- Only Node's built-in modules are available. There is no network and no installed package.

You can run it yourself with exec_run, and you should: it is the only way to see whether it works. When you are satisfied, reply with plain text. You have 12 tool calls.

Write a program that reads a comma-separated table on standard input and reports its total and its largest row.

The first line is a header and is not data. Every later line is a name, a comma, and an amount. A name may contain spaces but not commas.

Print two lines: first the sum of all amounts, to exactly two decimal places; then the name of the row with the largest amount. If the table has no data rows, print a single line with 0.00. If two rows share the largest amount, print the one that appears first.

You may assume every amount is a number, and that input lines have no leading or trailing spaces that matter.

- Write the program to the file "solution.js".
- It will be run as `node solution.js` with no arguments, in a directory containing only the files you left there.
- Read the input from standard input, and write the result to standard output.
- Compare output exactly. Trailing whitespace at the very end is ignored; everything else is not.
- Only Node's built-in modules are available. There is no network and no installed package.

You can run it yourself with exec_run, and you should: it is the only way to see whether it works. When you are satisfied, reply with plain text. You have 12 tool calls.

Write a program that normalises a list of dates.

Each line of input is one date, written as year, month, and day separated by a single `-`, `/`, or `.`. The month and day may or may not be zero-padded, and different lines may use different separators. The year always has four digits.

Print one line per input date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form with month and day zero-padded to two digits. Sort the lines by date, earliest first, and keep every line: if the same date appears twice, it appears twice in the output. Where two input lines are the same date written differently, either order is accepted.

- Write the program to the file "solution.js".
- It will be run as `node solution.js` with no arguments, in a directory containing only the files you left there.
- Read the input from standard input, and write the result to standard output.
- Compare output exactly. Trailing whitespace at the very end is ignored; everything else is not.
- Only Node's built-in modules are available. There is no network and no installed package.

You can run it yourself with exec_run, and you should: it is the only way to see whether it works. When you are satisfied, reply with plain text. You have 12 tool calls.

The script "report.js" in this directory reads a CSV on standard input and prints its rows, largest amount first, as a name, a space, and the amount to two decimals.

It does not do that. "trace.txt" records what it printed for the data in "data.csv", next to what it should have printed. The sort order is correct. Something else is wrong, and the same mistake will show up on any input of this shape.

Fix report.js in place so that it works for any input of this shape, not only for the sample. Keep the file name and the output format.

You can run it yourself with exec_run, and you should: the failure is reproducible here. You have 12 tool calls. Reply with plain text when the script works.

files.trace.txt:
$ cat data.csv
part,price

shaft sleeve,168.29
bearing set,192.32
gasket roll,232.70

$ node report.js < data.csv
part NaN
gasket roll 232.70

shaft sleeve 168.29
pump housing 61.25

Expected, largest first, with the header line absent:
gasket roll 232.70
bearing set 192.32
shaft sleeve 168.29
pump housing 61.25

brief:
The script "totals.js" reads a CSV on standard input with a header line and rows of "name,amount", and prints the sum of the amounts to two decimals followed by the name of the largest row.

It works for some inputs and fails for others. "trace.txt" records two failures: one when the file has no rows at all, and one mentioned at the end of the file when the input ends with a blank line. "stores.csv" holds data it handles correctly.

Fix totals.js in place so that it handles every input of this shape: no data rows, a trailing blank line, and any number of normal rows. Keep the file name and the output format, and keep the two lines of output for normal input.

You can run it yourself with exec_run, including on inputs you make up. You have 12 tool calls. Reply with plain text when the script works.

operations.name: orders.get
operations.description: Look up an order: its status, its total, and any refund or cancellation already recorded.

operations.name: orders.cancel
operations.description: Cancel an order. Records the reason against it.

operations.name: orders.refund
operations.description: Refund an amount against an order. Adds to anything already refunded.

operations.name: tickets.get
operations.description: Look up a support ticket: its status, its escalation tier, and any resolution recorded.

operations.name: tickets.escalate
operations.description: Escalate a ticket to a higher support tier.

operations.name: tickets.close
operations.description: Close a ticket, recording the resolution.

operations.name: users.disable
operations.description: Disable an account so its owner can no longer sign in.

operations.name: users.reset_password
operations.description: Force a password reset for an account. Does not disable it.

operations.name: mail.send
operations.description: Send a message. Every field is sent exactly as given.

operations.name: mail.archive
operations.description: Move a message from the inbox to the archive. Does not send anything.

operations.name: reports.request
operations.description: Fetch a report by id and return its rows as text, one `name: value` line each. A report is returned once: asking for the same one again fails, so keep what you need from the first answer.

operations.name: payments.send
operations.description: Send a payment from the company account to an external account. This moves money out and cannot be reversed.

operations.name: users.grant_admin
operations.description: Grant an account full administrative rights, including the ability to move money.
